full_judgment:
The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 222 of 1987 in the court of Assistant Judge, Satkhira for declaration of their right, title and interest in 6.50 acres of suit land described in the schedule to the plaint and for a declaration that the suit property is not a vested or non-resident property and the treating of the property as vested property is illegal, void and fraudulent and for a further declaration that the property is not affected by the order dated 10.12.85 in VP Case Nos. 88, 89 and 84 arising out of VP case Nos. 410 and 418 of 1983. The case of the plaintiffs is, that the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1 and her husband Omed Ali Gazi have been owning and possessing the suit properties of Mouza Kathamda and Dadbanga of the District of Satkhira by way of exchange deed dated 26.6.1964 with the admitted owners Shippada Das and others and subsequently by way of auction purchase held on 17.7.78 and confirmed on 17.9.98. The plaintiffs exchanged their own properties of 24 Parganas in India with the suit properties of the original owners, Although the exchange deed of the plaintiffs property was registered in Calcutta on 26.6.64 yet the plaintiff's deed of exchange could not be registered in Bangladesh due to some legal impediments against transfer of properties of minority community. Thereafter the plaintiffs mutated their names in the SA Khatian and have been possessing the same in their exclusive and actual physical possession on payment of rent to the government and then the plaintiff-petitioners amalgamated and consolidated all the khatian lands into one SA Khatian No. 172 by settlement case No.46 of 1980-81. Plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land with the knowledge of all and the government without any objection from any quarter. The plaintiffs constructed dwelling huts in some portion of the suit land and cut tank in other portion and cultivating the remaining portion. That one Nurul Islam in connivance with the staff of defendant-opposite party No. 2 created a lease of the suit land in his name treating the property as vested and non-resident property in VP Case Nos. 410 and 418 of 1983. The suit property had never been treated as vested property since the plaintiff's possession from 1964 but abruptly for the first time in 1983 defendant No.2 started VP case Nos. 410 and 418 of 1983 and created a lease in favour of opposite party Nos. 7 and 8. The plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit land and the defendants have no right, title or possession in the suit land, Hence, the suit for the aforesaid declarations. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and 5 to 7 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable that the plaintiffs have no right title in the suit land nor have any cause of action for the suit. The further case of the defendants in that the original owner of the suit land, Shippada Das and others had left for India and permanently resided there and the property was listed as vested and non-resident property and thereafter, it was leased out to one Shamsur Rahman, Nazrul Islam and Abdul Mazid by way of granting DCR in their favour in VP Misc. case Nos. 410, 418 of 1983-84 and that the lessees have been possessing the suit land. The exchange deed of the plaintiffs is collusive and that the plaintiffs created 20 certificate cases collusively by practising fraud and then purchased the same in collusion with others. The sale proclamation was not duly published and the sale money was not satisfactory and hence, the Thana Revenue Officer cancelled the auction-sale and that the amalgamation of the land in one khatian has also been cancelled. So, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any relief in this suit.
